```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

## Model

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_i &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma) \\
\mu_i &= a + b x_i \\
a &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 0.2) \\
b &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 0.5) \\
\sigma &\sim \text{Exponential}(1)
\end{aligned}
$$

- Data model and priors from post 2.
- $x_i$: family SES (`parent_ses_z`), the real values.
- $y_i$: simulated adult SES. The real outcome is not used.

## True values

```{r}
#| label: truth

true_intercept <- 0
true_slope <- 0.4
true_sigma <- sqrt(1 - true_slope^2)

truth <- tibble(
  parameter = factor(c("Intercept", "Slope", "Residual SD"), c("Intercept", "Slope", "Residual SD")),
  value = c(true_intercept, true_slope, true_sigma)
)
mutate(truth, value = round(value, 3))
```

- Intercept `r true_intercept`: the outcome is standardized.
- Slope `r true_slope`: Blau and Duncan's correlation.
- Residual SD $\sqrt{1 - b^2}$ = `r sprintf("%.2f", true_sigma)`: the outcome
  SD is then 1.

## Simulated data

```{r}
#| label: fake-data

mobility <- read_mobility()

fake <- tibble(parent_ses_z = mobility$parent_ses_z) |>
  slice_sample(prop = 1) |>
  mutate(fake_adult_ses = simulate_regression(parent_ses_z, true_intercept, true_slope, true_sigma))

fake_ols <- lm(fake_adult_ses ~ parent_ses_z, fake)

tibble(
  Students = nrow(fake),
  `SD of y` = sd(fake$fake_adult_ses),
  `Correlation of x and y` = cor(fake$parent_ses_z, fake$fake_adult_ses),
  `OLS slope` = coef(fake_ols)[["parent_ses_z"]]
) |>
  mutate(across(-Students, \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-fake-data
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

sizes <- c(20, 100, 1000, nrow(fake))
size_labels <- paste("n =", format(sizes, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))

fake_subsets <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(sizes), \(i) {
  mutate(fake[seq_len(sizes[i]), ], size = size_labels[i])
})) |>
  mutate(size = factor(size, size_labels))

ggplot(fake_subsets, aes(parent_ses_z, fake_adult_ses)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(intercept = true_intercept, slope = true_slope, colour = okabe_ito[1], linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~size, nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Family SES (standardized)",
    y = "Simulated adult SES",
    title = "Simulated data and the true line, first n students"
  )
```

- Real family SES values in random order; each fit uses the first $n$.
- Simulated outcome SD `r sprintf("%.3f", sd(fake$fake_adult_ses))`;
  correlation `r sprintf("%.3f", cor(fake$parent_ses_z, fake$fake_adult_ses))`.
- Full-sample OLS slope `r sprintf("%.3f", coef(fake_ols)[["parent_ses_z"]])`
  vs. true `r true_slope`.

## Recovery

```{r}
#| label: recovery
#| message: false

model_formula <- fake_adult_ses ~ 0 + Intercept + parent_ses_z
model_priors <- slope_prior("parent_ses_z", center = 0, sd = 0.5, intercept_sd = 0.2)
parameters <- c(Intercept = "b_Intercept", Slope = "b_parent_ses_z", `Residual SD` = "sigma")

recovery <- recovery_sweep(fake, model_formula, model_priors, sizes, parameters) |>
  left_join(truth, by = "parameter") |>
  mutate(covers = low <= value & value <= high)

recovery |>
  mutate(
    across(c(mean, low, high), \(x) round(x, 3)),
    n = format(n, big.mark = ",")
  ) |>
  select(n, Parameter = parameter, Truth = value, `Posterior mean` = mean, `2.5%` = low, `97.5%` = high, `Covers truth` = covers)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-recovery
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

ggplot(recovery, aes(n, mean)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = value), truth, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), width = 0.15) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = sizes, labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Students",
    y = "Posterior mean and 95% interval",
    title = "Posterior for each parameter by sample size",
    caption = "Dashed line: the value the data were simulated from."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: recovery-values

slope_at <- function(size) filter(recovery, parameter == "Slope", n == size)
width_at <- function(size) slope_at(size)$high - slope_at(size)$low
```

- Intervals that cover the truth: `r sum(recovery$covers)` of `r nrow(recovery)`.
- Slope, n = 20: `r sprintf("%.2f", slope_at(20)$mean)`
  (`r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", slope_at(20)$low, slope_at(20)$high)`).
- Slope, n = `r format(nrow(fake), big.mark = ",")`:
  `r sprintf("%.3f", slope_at(nrow(fake))$mean)`
  (`r sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", slope_at(nrow(fake))$low, slope_at(nrow(fake))$high)`).
- Slope interval width: `r sprintf("%.2f", width_at(20))` at n = 20;
  `r sprintf("%.2f", width_at(100))` at 100; `r sprintf("%.3f", width_at(1000))`
  at 1,000; `r sprintf("%.3f", width_at(nrow(fake)))` at the full sample.
- One simulated data set. Repeating with many data sets checks coverage.

## Prior sensitivity

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity
#| message: false

slope_priors <- list(
  "Normal(0, 10)" = slope_prior("parent_ses_z", center = 0, sd = 10, intercept_sd = 0.2),
  "Normal(0, 0.5)" = model_priors,
  "Normal(0, 0.1)" = slope_prior("parent_ses_z", center = 0, sd = 0.1, intercept_sd = 0.2)
)

sensitivity <- prior_sweep(
  fake, fake_adult_ses ~ parent_ses_z, model_formula, "parent_ses_z", slope_priors, sizes
) |>
  filter(Fit != "OLS") |>
  mutate(Fit = droplevels(Fit))

sensitivity |>
  select(n, Fit, Estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Fit, values_from = Estimate) |>
  mutate(across(-n, \(x) round(x, 3)), n = format(n, big.mark = ","))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sensitivity
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5

ggplot(sensitivity, aes(n, Estimate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = true_slope, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Low, ymax = High), width = 0.15) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~Fit, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = sizes, labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Students",
    y = "Slope",
    title = "Posterior mean and 95% interval of the slope, by slope prior and sample size",
    caption = "Dashed line: the true slope. Intercept Normal(0, 0.2) and residual SD Exponential(1) in all three."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity-values

sensitivity_at <- function(size, prior) filter(sensitivity, n == size, Fit == prior)$Estimate

# The largest gap between the three priors' posterior means at each size
prior_gap <- function(size) diff(range(filter(sensitivity, n == size)$Estimate))
round(sapply(sizes, prior_gap), 3) |> setNames(format(sizes, big.mark = ","))
```

- Normal(0, 10): wide. Normal(0, 0.5): the post 2 choice. Normal(0, 0.1):
  95% of its mass within ±0.2, so 0.4 is unlikely under it.
- n = 20, posterior mean of the slope:
  Normal(0, 10) `r sprintf("%.2f", sensitivity_at(20, "Normal(0, 10)"))`;
  Normal(0, 0.5) `r sprintf("%.2f", sensitivity_at(20, "Normal(0, 0.5)"))`;
  Normal(0, 0.1) `r sprintf("%.2f", sensitivity_at(20, "Normal(0, 0.1)"))`.
- n = 1,000: Normal(0, 0.1) `r sprintf("%.3f", sensitivity_at(1000, "Normal(0, 0.1)"))`
  vs. Normal(0, 10) `r sprintf("%.3f", sensitivity_at(1000, "Normal(0, 10)"))`.
- Full sample: all three between
  `r sprintf("%.3f", min(filter(sensitivity, n == nrow(fake))$Estimate))` and
  `r sprintf("%.3f", max(filter(sensitivity, n == nrow(fake))$Estimate))`.
- Largest gap between the three: `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_gap(20))` at n = 20;
  `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_gap(100))` at 100; `r sprintf("%.3f", prior_gap(1000))`
  at 1,000; `r sprintf("%.3f", prior_gap(nrow(fake)))` at the full sample.

## Summary

- Simulated from known values: $a$ = `r true_intercept`, $b$ = `r true_slope`,
  $\sigma$ = `r sprintf("%.2f", true_sigma)`.
- Every 95% interval covers its true value (`r sum(recovery$covers)` of `r nrow(recovery)`).
- Slope interval width: `r sprintf("%.2f", width_at(20))` at n = 20,
  `r sprintf("%.3f", width_at(nrow(fake)))` at the full sample.
- Gap between slope priors: `r sprintf("%.2f", prior_gap(20))` at n = 20,
  `r sprintf("%.3f", prior_gap(nrow(fake)))` at the full sample.
- Next: the same model on the real outcome.
